newsitem.title: USA: PENNCORP DECLINES COMMENT ON DEAL.
newsitem.headline: PENNCORP DECLINES COMMENT ON DEAL.

text.p: PennCorp Financial Group Inc declined to comment on shareholder opposition to its proposed acquisition of Washington National Corp.

Paulson & Co, an investment management firm with a 6.2 percent stake in Washington National, said it opposes the life insurer's proposed merger with PennCorp, calling the terms of the deal "inadequate."
When asked whether the company might revise its offer, PennCorp again declined to comment.
PennCorp agreed in November to acquire Washington National for $29.50 a share in cash and stock in a deal valued at $400 million.
In May, the companies agreed to extend the completion date of their merger to August 30.
In November, Washington National said it expected the merger to be completed in the first quarter of 1997.
The deal has been delayed as the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has continued to hold up approval of the companies' proxy statements.
The revised merger agreement also allows PennCorp the right to increase the cash portion of the purchase price consideration to a maximum of 45 percent of the transaction value.
Washington National spokesman Craig Simundza said it considered Paulson's opposition to the deal as one shareholder's viewpoint.
When asked whether Washington National considered the terms of the deal inadequate, Simundza said "we have an agreement."
